editorial:
Imagine moving from a small town to the big city of Bucharest and trying to fit in at a fancy high school. That is exactly what happens to Mihai, a smart kid who loves math and philosophy. He thinks his books are the most important thing in the world until he meets Dana, a girl who is a total pro at chess. The vibe of this movie is sweet and cozy, capturing that awkward but exciting feeling of being sixteen and falling in love for the first time. You will feel like you are right there in the classroom with them, dealing with teachers and the pressure of school while trying to sneak in a few romantic moments.

What really works here is how natural the acting feels. It does not feel like a staged play; it feels like real teenagers talking. The pacing is steady, though some parts move a bit slow, but the chemistry between the leads keeps you interested. If you love old-school romances that focus on heart rather than explosions, you should definitely check this out. Since it is an older gem, you might want to look for a restored version to add the 4K Blu-ray to your physical collection or see if you can find a high-quality digital rental on Apple TV to get the best picture.
endingExplained: After facing plenty of arguments and school stress, Mihai and Dana finally put their differences aside. They realize that their love is stronger than their academic goals or their pride. The movie ends with them choosing each other over their individual obsessions. It wraps up on a happy note, showing that while school is important, the friendships and romantic bonds you make are what you actually remember years later.
targetAudience: Ideal for anyone who loves cute 80s romance and coming-of-age stories.
